question: How much of a modern CNN's spatial filtering must be learned if trainable pointwise convolutions can form linear combinations of a sufficiently large frozen random filter bank?

key_findings.claim: Off-the-shelf CNNs separate into architectures that tolerate frozen random spatial filters and architectures that fail badly, with pointwise combinations explaining much of the split.
key_findings.evidence: On CIFAR-10, bottleneck-style ResNet-50/101, Wide-ResNet, and MobileNet variants lose only 1.6-1.9 points while models without comparable post-spatial 1x1 mixing lose at least 16; ImageNet exhibits a similar architectural pattern.

key_findings.claim: A pointwise convolution after a spatial convolution exactly parameterizes linear combinations of the earlier spatial kernels when no intervening nonlinear operation breaks the algebra.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 3.1 rewrites the two linear convolutions as one effective spatial kernel; the LC-block uses an expansion E to control the number of frozen random basis filters while retaining the same forward expressivity after folding.

key_findings.claim: At high expansion, frozen-random LC networks match or outperform trainable spatial-filter baselines on the tested small-image tasks.
key_findings.evidence: CIFAR-10 frozen-random models surpass the learnable LC variant near E=8 and the unmodified baseline near E=128; CIFAR-100, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN results at E=128 are on par or slightly higher across four runs.

anchors.section: 4.1 Increasing the rate of linear combinations

key_findings.claim: The advantage is not established at practical ImageNet scale or under strong robustness evaluation.
key_findings.evidence: The ImageNet expansion sweep uses one run and does not beat the baseline; the robustness result is only low-budget FGSM at epsilon 1/255, and the paper explicitly says it is no match for adversarial training or high-budget attacks.

key_findings.claim: Large kernels expose a structural limitation of i.i.d. random bases.
key_findings.evidence: The random bank's spatial variance remains uniform, whereas learned large kernels concentrate weight near the center; increasing expansion eventually closes the tested accuracy gap but cannot efficiently reproduce sharp central structure.

key_findings.claim: Claims that learning spatial filters hurts are confounded by parameterization and optimization rather than expressivity alone.
key_findings.evidence: Learnable LC-blocks and frozen LC-blocks have different trainable subspaces and implicit regularization; the paper observes that an identity-equivalent parameterization learns worse representations but does not isolate optimizer conditioning, matched compute, or regularization strength.

method.core_idea: Freeze spatial convolution kernels at random initialization and learn only downstream linear combinations, then vary explicit LC expansion, architecture width, depth, and kernel size to test when the random bank spans useful effective filters.
method.mechanism: Insert a spatial convolution with E-times more outputs followed immediately by a trainable 1x1 convolution, omit intervening normalization/nonlinearity for exact folding, and compare frozen versus jointly learned spatial banks under otherwise matched ResNet designs.
assumptions: A sufficiently large random filter bank spans the effective spatial kernels needed by the task.
The no-intermediate-operation LC-block represents behavior of modern bottleneck architectures.
Validation gains at high expansion outweigh the added activation and compute costs.
Filter variance entropy is meaningfully connected to generalization and robustness.
Optimizer settings are comparably suitable for frozen and fully learnable parameterizations.

techniques.role: Supplies a fixed random basis with a spatial inductive bias.
Learns effective convolution filters as channel-wise combinations of the random bank.
Controls basis overcompleteness independently of output width.
Compares learned and recombined filters in the common spatial-kernel space.
Quantifies diversity or collapse of convolutional filter patterns.

evaluations.setting: Off-the-shelf CNN architectures on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
evaluations.metric: Validation accuracy gap between learned and frozen spatial convolutions.
evaluations.result: Architectures with substantial 1x1 mixing retain much more accuracy; ResNet-18 is a notable failure case.
evaluations.baseline: Normally trained versions of each architecture.

evaluations.setting: ResNet-LC-20-16 on CIFAR-10 across E, width, and depth.
evaluations.metric: Clean accuracy, low-budget FGSM accuracy, and learnable parameter count.
evaluations.result: Frozen random networks eventually overtake learnable LC and unmodified baselines as the number of combinations grows.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified ResNet and learnable LC-block variants over at least four seeds.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN at E=128.
evaluations.result: Frozen random variants are on par with or modestly above the baseline in the reported four-run comparisons.
Frozen random E=64 reaches 72.46/90.57 versus 72.60/90.69 for the shown learnable baseline; all are single runs.

evaluations.metric: Accuracy gap and effective-kernel spatial variance.
evaluations.result: Larger kernels require more expansion; random combinations preserve uniform spatial variance unlike learned center-heavy kernels.
evaluations.baseline: Learnable spatial convolutions at matched architecture settings.

limitations: Author-stated: experiments cover image classification and primarily ResNet-family models.
Author-stated: conclusions may differ under non-gradient optimizers and non-pointwise forms of linear combination.
Reviewer inference: high LC expansion reduces trainable spatial parameters but can substantially increase activations and multiply-adds; end-to-end efficiency is not the evaluation target.
Reviewer inference: ImageNet comparisons use one seed and do not demonstrate superiority.
Reviewer inference: the robustness evidence uses only a weak single-step attack.
Reviewer inference: FVE correlations do not identify why joint training underperforms.
failure_modes: The random basis is too small relative to kernel dimension or task complexity.
Intervening ReLU, normalization, attention, or grouping breaks exact linear folding.
Random large-kernel bases need prohibitive expansion to express localized spatial structure.
Memory and compute from expanded feature maps erase any savings in learnable parameters.
Jointly learnable LC factors suffer ill-conditioning or harmful implicit bias under the chosen optimizer.
Frozen bases fail under distribution shift even when in-distribution classification remains competitive.
reusable_insights: Architectural 1x1 mixing can hide how little task-specific spatial filtering is required.
Exact forward expressivity does not imply equivalent optimization or implicit regularization under a factorized parameterization.
Parameter-count savings must be separated from activation memory, arithmetic cost, and latency.
Structured fixed bases are a direct next baseline when i.i.d. filters waste capacity on unhelpful spatial directions.
open_questions: Can learned initialization distributions or analytic filter banks achieve the same accuracy with far smaller expansion?
Do frozen spatial banks remain competitive for detection, segmentation, video, audio, or scientific fields?
What optimizer or regularizer prevents degeneration when both LC factors are trainable?
How do frozen bases behave under strong adaptive attacks and natural corruptions?
What is the quality-compute frontier after kernel folding at inference and expanded activations during training?

competitive_landscape.title: Local Binary Convolutional Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: LBCNN already combines fixed sparse binary filter responses with learned linear weights; the reviewed paper uses dense random spatial banks and systematically studies expansion, depth, width, and exact pre-activation linear folding.

competitive_landscape.title: Training BatchNorm and Only BatchNorm: On the Expressive Power of Random Features in CNNs
competitive_landscape.difference: Frankle et al. train only affine normalization parameters throughout otherwise random CNNs; the reviewed work isolates trainable 1x1 combinations and spatial-filter freezing.

competitive_landscape.title: Convolutional Neural Networks Do Work with Pre-Defined Filters
competitive_landscape.difference: PFCNN replaces large i.i.d. banks with a small repeated pool of predefined filters plus 1x1 mixing, directly pursuing the efficiency and structure left open by the reviewed work.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Generalization in Convolutional Neural Networks through Regularization with Edge and Line Features
competitive_landscape.difference: Linse et al. deliberately bias fixed filters toward edges and lines for small-data generalization; the reviewed work chooses unbiased random filters to analyze representational sufficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: The Quest for Universal Master Key Filters in DS-CNNs
competitive_landscape.difference: Babaiee et al. extract eight reusable Gaussian-derivative-like filters and report over 80 percent ImageNet accuracy in depthwise-separable CNNs, challenging the need for the reviewed paper's very large random expansions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Sufficient linear combinations make learned spatial convolutions unnecessary and sometimes harmful in many contemporary CNNs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: An exact algebraic lemma, controlled LC-block sweeps, multiple small datasets, off-the-shelf architecture comparisons, and effective-filter analyses support a restricted version of the claim.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The systematic expansion study and architecture diagnosis are useful, but fixed-filter-plus-linear-combination networks predate the work. The evidence supports representational sufficiency under large overcomplete banks more strongly than practical efficiency or a general claim that learning filters is harmful.

reviewer_notes: Read all 20 extracted pages, including supplementary ablations, combined-filter figures, and compute accounting. Competitors were checked at primary OpenReview and arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
